prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, through ligand design and mechanistic understanding of amine arylation

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B069 for Buchwald and Hartwig as a single part. After the full first-round exchange, the case still rests on the three things I weigh most. First, the chemistry is established by structural and kinetic evidence, not only by scope tables: isolated oxidative-addition, amine-binding and reductive-elimination intermediates, and the ligand-design logic (bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphines) that those studies explain. Second, the method enabled a whole community to build bonds it could not build before, and it has been used daily for more than twenty-five years in pharmaceutical process chemistry, agrochemicals and organic electronic materials. Third, the credit is the cleanest on the shortlist: two people who independently and in parallel delivered the decisive general catalysts. The chair's summary confirms that no member disputes B069's maturity or attribution; the only objection is novelty relative to 2010, and I think that objection is answerable in the citation, which should name the C-N bond and the ligand and mechanistic basis so that it is plainly not a restatement of C-C coupling.
statement.case_against: The strongest case against my position is the one the chair identified: a prize to Buchwald and Hartwig will be read by some as an extension of the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize, and the best-known contribution is iterative ligand optimisation rather than a new concept. B045 offers a new modality with a clear chemical principle (induced proximity), the largest explicit support in round 1 (three members) and six of eight members placing it in their first choice or alternatives. If the committee decides that novelty of capability must outweigh attribution and maturity, B045 is the more defensible plurality choice, though only if its credit and clinical-maturity problems can be resolved honestly. The Kosugi and Migita precursor question also remains open from my side because I am relying on recall of the 1994 to 1995 chronology.

responses.point: The chair argues that degradation adds a mode of action whereas C-N coupling refines a bond construction the 2010 prize already framed, and asks whether the committee values attribution cleanliness over novelty of capability; he keeps B069 as first alternative.
responses.response: I accept the framing but not the equivalence. The 2010 prize rewarded coupling of carbon nucleophiles with organometallic partners. Amine coupling required different mechanistic solutions: amine binding and deprotonation at palladium, suppression of beta-hydride elimination, and a C-N reductive elimination that is intrinsically harder than C-C. These were solved by ligand design that was tested on isolated intermediates. I do agree that a modality is a larger step than a better route to a known bond. My answer is that a Nobel Prize does not need to be the largest novelty on the list. It needs a clear principle, independent confirmation and defensible credit, and on the last two B069 is clearly ahead of B045 today.

responses.point: Chabes prefers B045 over B069 because degraders open a new modality, while C-N coupling risks being seen as an extension after the 2010 and 2021 prizes. He says he could be persuaded if the committee weights clean attribution above breadth of consequence.
responses.response: This is a fair statement of the real disagreement, and I do not think the answer is a count of supporters. I agree that the mechanistic evidence for degradation (ternary-complex structures, cooperativity, kinetics) is good, and I take seriously his argument that cereblon is different in kind from later optimisation. My difficulty is how the citation could be written. Crews and Deshaies conceived and proved the PROTAC concept, while Handa identified cereblon as the target of a drug already in clinical use, which is a mechanistic discovery rather than a designed concept. A three-name prize leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito, each with a structural or proof-of-concept claim. As a structural chemist I would be uncomfortable with a citation that rewards the idea but not the structures of ternary complexes that show how it works. I therefore keep B069 first, and I would support B045 if the committee reaches a defensible credit boundary.

responses.point: Aili argues that induced proximity is a designable chemical principle and that B045 is a broadly acceptable anchor, and notes that the glue branch is clinically mature while PROTACs are not.
responses.response: I agree with his own observation that the glue branch is already clinically mature, since it makes the best argument for maturity, but it is also the branch whose credit sits with Handa, who identified cereblon, and arguably Ito, rather than with the PROTAC concept. That reinforces my view that the case is two achievements joined under one heading. If the committee wanted a two-part prize, the least arbitrary version would give the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism separate parts, but the three-person cap then leaves one name for one part, which I find hard to defend. I do not yet see that B045 is cleaner than B069 for a final ballot.

responses.point: Somfai holds B069 first and, in his round-1 reply to me, says he is less settled than I am on B054 because the trio is arbitrary (Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi have comparable claims) and MacMillan already has the 2021 prize.
responses.response: His point on B054 is correct and I have moved on it: the attribution is arbitrary and the 2021 overlap is real, so I no longer treat B054 as a serious second part, only as a distant alternative. On B069 we agree about Kosugi, and I add that because the committee lacks an expert report on the tin-amide chronology, the safest course is to name only the two who developed the general catalysts. We should state in the citation that it is the generality and the ligand-based catalyst design that is being recognised.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B006 for Gray and Winkler as a bounded two-person attribution with a quantitative principle, and asks what a citation would add that Marcus's did not.
responses.response: I respect the quantitative case and maintain my round-1 view that B006 is a mechanistic insight in a narrower community which builds on the 1992 Marcus prize. His question about what a citation would tell a broad audience is, in my view, the weakest point of B006 and is the reason I do not move it into my configuration. If the committee wants a second part, I would still not object to B006, but I do not think the case for a two-part prize has been made.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee will give the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize in judging C-N coupling as a distinct achievement.
Kosugi and Migita priority: I rely on memory for the 1994 to 1995 chronology, and an expert report would be needed to be certain. My current position is to credit only Buchwald and Hartwig.

Whether a two-part prize (for example B069 with B045) would be less arbitrary than a single part, given that the three-person cap would force one laureate in the second part and no defensible single name exists for B045.
Whether B045 will be judged mature enough without an approved degrader, and where Ciulli should sit if the committee does move to it; I cannot verify the clinical status independently.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need has arisen for B069, B045 or B054. B013 (serial femtosecond crystallography) touches my own field of electron crystallography, but I have no personal or institutional tie to its credited names, and it is no longer in my configuration. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate. I am also not aware of any tie to any credited name on B045 or B069.
